speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; to help me determine the cause, could you please tell me exactly where the pain is located and how it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis (with possible underlying inflammatory arthritis).

Please confirm if you have noticed any swelling, redness, or morning stiffness in your fingers or wrists, and have you ever experienced numbness or tingling in your thumb or index finger? REQUEST TEST: Blood work (ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor, Anti-CCP).
